key_points.point: The document proposes replacing legacy centralized healthcare IT architectures with a dynamic, decentralized 'living' AI backbone that integrates edge computing and blockchain. By shifting to a Data-Centric AI model, the framework optimizes the quality of training data through human-in-the-loop validation, ensuring robust global model performance. This approach accelerates the deployment of automated healthcare environments in resource-constrained settings by reducing reliance on expensive, centralized cloud infrastructure. The authors acknowledge that this decentralized model introduces higher system latency compared to centralized servers, which they accept as a necessary trade-off for achieving a trustless, scalable audit trail.
key_points.verbatim: To address these limitations, we propose a novel decentralized framework that synergizes ôFederated Learning (FL)ö with ôData-Centric AIö principles. ... By incorporating human-in-the-loop validation (e.g., nurse verification of fall events), our system ensures that the local models are trained on high-quality, verified labels, thereby improving the robustness of the global model without compromising privacy.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Replace legacy centralized healthcare IT with adaptive, decentralized AI infrastructure to enable scalable, low-cost automated monitoring.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that advocates for replacing legacy IT architectures with a dynamic, adaptive 'living' AI backbone. Encompasses: integration of all data types, real-time edge computing, and decentralized model aggregation.

key_points.point: The document introduces a feedback mechanism where human verification (e.g., nurse confirmation of fall events) is cryptographically signed and used to update the reputation score of edge nodes. This reputation score then weights the influence of that node's model updates on the global model, effectively filtering out noise from faulty sensors.

The document mandates the use of cryptographically signed 'Proofs of Quality' to create an immutable clinical audit trail for medical liability. By replacing a central aggregator with a consortium blockchain, the system ensures that all model updates are traceable and verifiable, preventing opaque 'black box' model poisoning. This mechanism provides a liability-ready record for clinical misdiagnoses, addressing the safetyist concern regarding the lack of auditability in standard federated learning. The authors note that this approach requires higher system latency, which they justify as a critical legal requirement for healthcare environments.
key_points.verbatim: We extend the blockchainÆs utility beyond mere aggregation (as seen in Sheller et al. (2020)) to generate cryptographically signed ôProofs of Quality,ö providing a liability-ready audit trail for clinical misdiagnoses.
key_points.canonical_proposition: Mandate cryptographically signed audit trails for all AI model updates to ensure clinical accountability and prevent deniable misuse.
key_points.attribution_text: An Intention within safetyist discourse that requires cryptographically signed, subject-keyed inference logs with built-in privacy-preserving constraints. Encompasses: zero-knowledge proof generation, immutable audit trails, and clinical liability tracking.

key_points.point: The document seeks to enforce strict boundaries on corporate data extraction by keeping sensitive patient data local on edge devices, thereby preventing the non-consensual commodification of personal information. By utilizing a Data-Centric AI approach, the framework ensures that patient data remains local while model updates are cryptographically verified, addressing the skeptic concern regarding data sovereignty and privacy. The authors explicitly state that their framework resolves conflicts with GDPR 'Right to Erasure' mandates through data minimization, as the immutable ledger stores only abstracted model weights rather than raw patient data. This approach prioritizes individual data autonomy while maintaining the utility of the healthcare monitoring system.
key_points.verbatim: While Federated Learning addresses privacy concerns by keeping sensitive patient data on local devices, it often faces challenges regarding data heterogeneity and quality at the edge. ... Our framework resolves this inherently through Data Minimization. The immutable ledger stores only neural network weights, cryptographic hashes, and verification flags, not Protected Health Information (PHI) or raw images.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section 1, Introduction and Section 4.4, Regulatory compliance
key_points.canonical_proposition: Enforce strict boundaries on corporate data extraction by keeping sensitive patient data local and using data minimization techniques.
key_points.attribution_text: A Desire within skeptic discourse that seeks to enforce strict boundaries on corporate data extraction and prevent the non-consensual commodification of personal information for model training. Encompasses: data sovereignty, privacy-preserving federated learning, and data minimization.

factual_claims.claim: The proposed L-CNN architecture reduces FLOPs by approximately 85% compared to standard VGG-like blocks, enabling real-time inference on mid-range smartphone NPUs.
Standard VGG16 architecture resulted in an average battery drain of 14.2% per hour on a Huawei P30 Pro, while the proposed L-CNN reduced this to 3.1% per hour.
